concepts.def: Hierarchical division of society into ranked groups based on power, wealth and status.
Davis and Moore (1945): inequality is necessary to motivate the most talented into the most important roles.
Society polarised into bourgeoisie (own means of production) and proletariat (sell labour); class conflict drives history.
Stratification involves class (economic), status (prestige) and party (power); more nuanced than Marx.
Weber's term for opportunities to gain valued resources (health, education, income) shaped by social position.
Measure of income inequality from 0 (perfect equality) to 1 (one person has all); UK around 0.36 (ONS).

walkthroughs.body_html:
The Sociology of Social Stratification — a core area of GCSE Sociology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

The Sociology of Social Stratification brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with The Sociology of Social Stratification.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Davis and Moore's functionalist theory argues inequality is:
options: Unnecessary
Necessary to motivate talent
A capitalist conspiracy
Disappearing

mcqs.q: Weber's three dimensions of stratification are class, status and:
options: Gender
Race
Party
Religion

mcqs.q: What do interpretivists seek when researching society?
options: Verstehen - understanding actors' subjective meanings.
To manipulate variables experimentally.
Statistical patterns and laws.
Both positivists and interpretivists prefer experiments above all else.

mcqs.q: Why do positivists and interpretivists prefer different methods?
options: Both positivists and interpretivists prefer experiments above all else.

Positivists treat sociology like natural science, seeking objective measurable patterns — preferring quantitative methods. Interpretivists believe humans construct meaning, requiring qualitative methods to access subjective experience.
To manipulate variables experimentally.
Positivists like numbers and interpretivists like words — that's the whole difference.

mcqs.q: What is the 'dark figure' of crime?
options: The amount of crime that is unreported or unrecorded.
Organised crime by criminal masterminds.
To manipulate variables experimentally.
Crimes committed at night.
